samples.summary: `POST .../slides` silently substitutes a different layout for an unknown `layoutId` instead of refusing it
samples.evidence: `addSlide` passes `layoutId` straight to `MemSlidesStore.addSlide`, whose `resolveLayout` (packages/slides/src/store/memory.ts:172-174) is `this.doc.layouts.find(...) ?? getLayout(layoutId)`, and `getLayout` (packages/slides/src/model/layout.ts:196-198) is `BUILT_IN_LAYOUTS.find(...) ?? BUILT_IN_LAYOUTS[0]`. So a typo'd or nonexistent layout id (`'title-boyd'`) returns 200 with a slide built from the *first* built-in layout, and the response's `id`/`index` give the caller no hint the layout was wrong. `ApiV1SlidesController.add` validates only that `layoutId` is a non-empty string (slides.controller.ts:110), and the whole point of the new `GET .../layouts` endpoint is that layout ids are a closed set the caller is expected to pick from — an id outside it should be a 400, not a silently different slide.

samples.summary: `DELETE /comments/:threadId` on a thread with an empty `comments` array 404s with "Comment not found", making such a thread permanently undeletable through the API
samples.evidence: `deleteThread`'s authorize callback computes `rootCommentId(thread)` = `copyThread(thread).comments[0]?.id`, which is `undefined` for a thread whose comment list is empty. `assertCommentAuthor` (line 527-528) then does `const comment = commentId ? findComment(...) : undefined; if (!comment) throw new NotFoundException('Comment not found')`. So the delete is refused with a 404 that names a comment, not the thread. `listThreads`/`isThread` happily surface such a thread (an empty CRDT array has numeric `length`, so `isThread` accepts it), so the API can *show* a thread it can never delete. Nothing in the write paths prevents an empty `comments` array arriving from a concurrent editor write or a partially-applied remote change — the ≥1-comment rule is only an invariant the writers maintain, not one this reader enforces.

samples.summary: `parsePdfAnchor` validates each rect component in 0..1 independently, so a region that runs off the page is accepted
samples.evidence: The loop checks `value < 0 || value > 1` per key but never `x + w <= 1` / `y + h <= 1`. `{ x: 0.9, y: 0.9, w: 0.9, h: 0.9 }` is accepted and stored, producing a `pdf-region` anchor that extends past the page edge — the viewer's highlight layer will render a box clipped to, or spilling out of, the page. The docblock claims the rectangle is "page-relative 0..1 units", which the stored value then violates.

samples.summary: In `notify`, the `planCommentNotifications` call sits outside the try/catch, so a throw there turns an already-committed comment write into a 500
samples.evidence: Lines 197-203 call `planCommentNotifications(...)` unguarded; only `notificationService.createFromComment` (line 206) is inside `try`. The method's own docblock says it is "Fire-and-forget ... a failed notification must never turn a successful write into an error for the caller", and the spec asserts exactly that for a service failure ('swallows a notification failure — the comment is already committed'). But the planner reads `thread.comments` and each `comment.author.userId` (notify-plan.ts:143 `String(c.author?.userId ?? '')` is guarded, though `extractMentionedUserIds(comment.body)` assumes `body` is a string); any throw from it propagates out of `createThread`/`reply`/`setResolved` after the CRDT write has already been synced, so the caller sees a 500 for a comment that exists.

samples.summary: `applySlideChange` can call `moveAfterByIndex(-1, from)` when a move targets the head of an array that exposes `moveAfterByIndex` but not `moveFront`
samples.evidence: The branch at lines 118-125 is entered when `slides.moveAfterByIndex && slides.getElementByIndex` are present. `moveFront` is only consulted inside `if (to === 0 && slides.moveFront)`; if `moveFront` is absent that condition is false and control falls to `else { slides.moveAfterByIndex(to - 1, from) }` with `to === 0`, i.e. `moveAfterByIndex(-1, from)` — an out-of-range predecessor index. All three methods are declared optional on `SlideArrayLike` (lines 78-80), so this combination is representable by the interface; the correct fallback for a headless move is the splice pair in the `else` at line 126.

samples.summary: `duplicateTab` copies `pivotTable` into the new worksheet, producing a second pivot-output tab bound to the same source that nothing regenerates
samples.evidence: `const copy: Worksheet = { ...worksheet, comments: {} };` strips only `comments`. A pivot *output* worksheet carries `pivotTable.sourceTabId` (read by `resolveDelete` at tab-ops.ts:87-88), so duplicating one yields a frozen copy of the pivot grid that still declares itself an output of the source tab. Two consequences: the copy's cells are a stale snapshot no pivot recompute owns, and `DELETE` on the source tab is now refused with `pivot_dependents` naming a tab the user never configured as a pivot (tabs.controller.ts:180-184). The controller only blocks duplication when the tab has no worksheet at all (tabs.controller.ts:246-251), so this path is reachable.

samples.summary: `parseImages` accepts A1 anchors that `parseRef` mis-parses (lowercase letters, range strings), storing an image anchored to a cell the caller did not name
samples.evidence: The anchor is validated by round-tripping through `parseRef` and only rejecting a thrown error. `parseRef` (packages/sheets/src/model/core/coordinates.ts:323-353) is lenient: it strips `$`, splits at the first digit and reduces the prefix with `char.charCodeAt(0) - 65 + 1`, so `'b2'` yields column 34 (98-65+1) rather than 2, and `'A1:B2'` yields `{r:1,c:1}` because `parseInt('1:B2') === 1`. Neither throws, so both are stored verbatim as `SheetImage.anchor` and the image lands on a cell 32 columns away, or on `A1` for what the caller wrote as a range. The same leniency reaches `sheetCellAnchor` in comments.controller.ts:649, where `'b2'` resolves `colOrder[33]` and usually produces a confusing "has no stable row/column id yet" 400 instead of "invalid reference".

samples.summary: `withSref` hands a live Yorkie array proxy to `cellAnchorToSref`, unlike every existing caller which detaches with `Array.from` first
samples.evidence: `withSref` passes `worksheet.rowOrder ?? []` and `worksheet.colOrder ?? []` straight into `cellAnchorToSref`, which calls `order.rowOrder.indexOf(anchor.rowId)` (packages/sheets/src/comment/anchor.ts:26-27). Both existing call sites detach first — `rowOrder: Array.from(ws.rowOrder ?? []) as string[]` at packages/frontend/src/app/documents/document-detail.tsx:276 and :763. If the array proxy does not expose `indexOf`, every `GET .../comments` and every sheet thread creation 500s. Counter-evidence I found: `root.tabOrder.indexOf(tabId)` is used on a live root proxy at document-detail.tsx:474, which suggests `indexOf` does exist and this is only a divergence from the established detach-first convention (plus an O(N) CRDT walk per thread on a dense axis). Flagging at low confidence for the verifier to settle.

samples.summary: `readBoardRoot` preserves an empty `meta.title`, which `assertValidBoardBody` then rejects — a GET→PUT round trip of such a board 400s
samples.evidence: `meta: { title: meta?.title ?? 'Untitled board' }` uses `??`, so a stored `title: ''` is returned as `''` rather than defaulted. `assertValidBoardBody` (docs-content.controller.ts:571-575) requires `typeof meta.title === 'string' && meta.title.length !== 0`, so piping `board content` back into `board set-content` — the exact workflow the CLI pair exists for — fails with "'meta.title' must be a non-empty string" for a board whose title was cleared.
